language.script_notes: English is the dominant signage language; Scottish Gaelic is increasingly visible on road signs, not only in the northwest and on the islands but also on main primary routes.
false_friends: Norway and Iceland (moorland and fjord-like sea lochs)

road_furniture.line_paint: As national; many single-track Highland roads use passing places marked with signs.
road_furniture.curb_style: As national; minimal roadside infrastructure in the Highlands.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national — mph signs and circular pole attachments; Highland single-track roads with diamond passing-place signs are a strong Scotland tell.

architecture.roof_style: Steep-pitched slate roofs on stone tenements; simple pitched roofs on crofts and farm buildings.
architecture.roof_material: Slate and corrugated metal; historically thatch on traditional blackhouses.
architecture.wall_construction: Thick solid-stone tenements three or four storeys high in Glasgow and Edinburgh; harled (rendered) stone walls on white-painted houses, particularly in the islands; grey granite in Aberdeen; low stone crofts and farmhouses in the Highlands.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Grey stone, white harling and dark slate roofs.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Four-storey stone tenements; whitewashed harled croft houses; stone castles and tower houses; single-track roads with passing places; sheep on unfenced roads.

nature.vegetation: Heather moorland, bracken, Caledonian pine forest and open, treeless hillsides with sheep; birch woodland in glens.
nature.terrain: Mountainous Highlands with deep glens and sea lochs, lowland central belt, and hundreds of islands (Hebrides, Orkney, Shetland).
nature.climate_signature: Cool, wet and windy, with dramatic cloud and mist over moor and loch.

vehicles.plate_color: As national — white front, yellow rear.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: 4x4 pickups and Land Rovers are common in rural areas; campervans on the North Coast 500 route.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good coverage of the central belt and main roads; even remote Highland and island single-track roads are largely covered.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national road furniture and plates
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Scotland has Gaelic signs on some roads, heather moorland and lochs, and grey-stone tenements; England lacks Gaelic and Wales shows bilingual Welsh-first signs.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Gaelic-language signage on the west coast, similar moor, coast and stone-wall landscape
confusion_set.tiebreaker: UK circular pole attachments, blue distance markers, mph speed signs and 'GIVE WAY' text separate Scotland from Ireland.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Moorland, bare hillsides, sea lochs comparable to fjords
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Scotland drives on the left with UK yellow rear plates and mph signs; Norway and Iceland drive on the right.
